definition: The right to obtain and reuse your personal data for your own purposes across different services, typically in a machine-readable format that can be transferred to another organization.
metaDescription: Data portability gives you the right to get your personal data from one service and move it to another. Learn how this privacy right works in practice.
simpleExplanation: Data portability means you can ask a company to give you all the personal data they have about you in a format that you can easily use elsewhere. It's like being able to take your contact list when you switch phone companies.
whyItMatters: Data portability prevents vendor lock-in and promotes competition by making it easier to switch services. It gives you control over your data and enables you to move between platforms without losing your information or starting over.
technicalDetail: Data portability requires organizations to provide personal data in structured, commonly used, and machine-readable formats like JSON, CSV, or XML. The data must be provided securely and include all personal data being processed, not just what's visible in user interfaces.

examples.explanation: You can download all your photos, posts, and friend lists from one social network and upload them to a different platform when switching services.
Your current email provider must give you all your emails, contacts, and calendar data in a format that your new email service can import.
You can request your viewing history, ratings, and preferences from one streaming platform to help personalize recommendations on a new service.
